about: A cell grows until something stops it: a wall the lock names, or the place where the next origin's claim is nearer than its own.
What stops it is never its own doing, so a cell alone between two walls is as wide as they leave it, and one that lands beside another takes the midpoint between them.
An origin landing beside a cell narrows that cell and never widens any.

cases.name: walls at 0, 30, 70 and 100 with origins at 12, 45, 48 and 90
